extracted.intended_audience: Companies and stakeholders subject to EU REACH (manufacturers, importers, downstream users, only representatives) and regulators/stakeholders seeking an overview of obligations
extracted.subtask_description: High-level explanatory guidance on the scope, actor responsibilities and core procedural elements of the EU REACH regulation (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction) for companies handling chemicals and articles placed on the EU market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of REACH applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, REACH applies to all chemical substances; not only those used in industrial processes but also in our day-to-day lives, for example in cleaning products, paints as well as in articles such as clothes, furniture and electrical appliances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation therefore has an impact on most companies across the EU — i.e. manufacturers, importers, downstream users and companies placing articles containing substances on the market. Consider whether the substance you handle falls within this broad scope (including substances in articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on companies
rubrics_metrics.description: REACH places the burden of proof on companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply with the regulation, companies must identify and manage the risks linked to the substances they manufacture and market in the EU. Companies are responsible for producing the necessary information and demonstrating compliance rather than regulators proving non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate safe use to ECHA
rubrics_metrics.description: They have to demonstrate to ECHA how the substance can be safely used, and they must communicate the risk management measures to the users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must provide information showing safe conditions of use and communicate appropriate risk management measures (for example via safety data sheets or other supply-chain communication). Documentation submitted to ECHA should enable assessment of safe use.

rubrics_metrics.name: If risks cannot be managed, authorities may restrict or ban and require substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the risks cannot be managed, authorities can restrict the use of substances in different ways. In the long run, the most hazardous substances should be substituted with less dangerous ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators can ban substances, restrict particular uses, or make uses subject to prior authorisation. Where possible, substitution with safer alternatives is the preferred long-term approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement and need to cooperate with other registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies need to register their substances and to do this they need to work together with other companies who are registering the same substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants of the same substance are expected to collaborate (e.g. joint submission, data sharing) to avoid unnecessary testing and to provide coherent information to ECHA. See ECHA guidance on joint submission and data-sharing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECHA compliance checks and Member State substance evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: ECHA receives and evaluates individual registrations for their compliance, and the EU Member States evaluate selected substances to clarify initial concerns for human health or for the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are two complementary assessment dimensions: dossier evaluation by ECHA to check registration completeness and compliance, and substance evaluation led by Member States to address concerns about specific substances. Registrants should expect both types of review and provide robust information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorities and scientific committees assess whether risks can be managed
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities and ECHA's scientific committees assess whether the risks of substances can be managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on restrictions, authorisation, or further regulatory action are informed by assessments from scientific committees and competent authorities evaluating risk management feasibility and sufficiency of measures proposed by industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined actor roles and associated responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, under REACH you may have one of these roles: Manufacturer; Importer; Downstream users; Only representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each role carries different responsibilities (e.g. manufacturers/importers typically register substances, downstream users must follow conditions of use and may need to communicate upstream/downstream). Actors must identify their role(s) and comply with the obligations relevant to that role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importers and only representatives bear REACH obligations for non-EU companies
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a company established outside the EU, you are not bound by the obligations of REACH... The responsibility for fulfilling the requirements of REACH, such as registration lies with the importers established in the European Union, or with the only representative of a non-EU manufacturer established in the European Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-EU manufacturers should appoint an EU-based importer or an Only Representative to fulfil REACH duties (registration, communication, etc.). Importers/only representatives must ensure registrations and compliance cover imported goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of alternative methods to reduce animal testing
rubrics_metrics.description: It also promotes alternative methods for the hazard assessment of substances in order to reduce the number of tests on animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should consider and apply alternative (non-animal) testing methods and share existing data to minimise animal testing, following ECHA guidance on testing strategies and alternatives.
